4. The defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4 contested the said suit by filing 3 sets of written statement denying all material allegation contending that the suit was not maintainable and the same was barred by limitation. The case of the defendant No.1, in short, was that the plaintiff creating some fictitious and fabricated documents and without paying any consideration, had filed the instant suit only to grab the valuable property. The defendant No.1 never proposed to sell the suit land and never executed any agreement and never put his signature in any sale deed. He also did not file any application before the House Building Finance Corporation to get permission to sell the suit land and never filed any application before the concerned office to get income tax and capital gain tax clearance certificates. The defendant No.1 filed an application in the office of defendant No. 2 on 8-2-72 stating that he was abducted by some unknown miscreants in the month of July, "72 and some persons forcibly obtained some signatures on some printed and on some blank papers. He apprehended that those miscreants might have tried to grab his property illegally and collusively. The sale deed is fictitious one and the story of execution of this sale deed is absolutely false. After submission of written statement, the defendant No.1 died and his heirs the defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(c) filed an additional written statement stating that the market price of the suit property at the relevant time was more than 4 lakh. They also stated that the prayer of specific performance of contract was not maintainable as the same was barred by limitation. 

 6. On consideration of the materials on record the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit directing the defendants to register sale deed as per provision under section 77 of the Registration Act. The learned trial Court held that the prayer for Specific Performance of Contract is barred by limitation. The opposite party Nos. 1(a) to 1(c) preferred appeal and the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. Then the plaintiff moved this Revisional application before this court and obtained the present Rule, 

 10. That is, no such bainanama was produced and proved. It appears from the plaint that on 5-8-1973 the plaintiff instituted the instant suit for a decree of direction under the provision of section 77 of the Registration Act upon the defendant to register the sale deed. Thereafter, on 20-3-78 a prayer was added for alternative decree of Specific Performance of Contract. Against such amendment the defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) preferred Civil Revision No. 933 of 1978. Although the said Rule was discharged but their Lordships allowed the defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(c) to file additional written statement. Accordingly, on 28-9-80 an additional written statement was filed by the defendant Nos.1(a) to 1(c) wherein they specifically stated that the prayer for specific performance of contract was not maintainable as the same was barred by limitation. Although the trial Court decreed the suit but held that the prayer for Specific Performance of Contract is barred by limitation. Against such finding the plaintiff did not file any cross objection before the appellate Court nor preferred any appeal. The learned appellate Court also considered the matter and on consideration of the materials on record came to the conclusion that the prayer for specific performance of contract is barred by limitation. I do not find anything wrong in the finding of the learned courts below. So, the petitioner is not entitled to get decree of specific performance of contract.
